initiative.title: Show the logic, not only the components, in TS/TSX data flow
initiative.summary: Make non-component code (helpers, hooks, handlers, server queries, transforms, state) visible in the TSX Data flow graph.
initiative.next_action: Merge the stack with gh stack merge; then run audit round 3 on visual-notes and retire

sources.anchor: see non TSX stuff in the data flow graph
scopeFor: scope has name and file only; classify()
Pro research prompt: dependency analysis and investigation UI
three boxes for doc: condense into a single box

claims.statement: Byron wants non-component code visible in the TS/TSX data-flow graph.
The graph reads as all components because folded functions use the grey value mark, which matches the component grey, and frames carry no role.
The goal is to see how data is reshaped, stored and handed across the server line, with components as one stop.
Folding and merging must keep the witness for each claim.
Two equal jobs: follow a full route, and spider out from a known symbol to what it touches or depends on.
Emphasize the symbols involved and how they relate and depend on each other.
Must show transforms, state containers and the server boundary; plain helpers matter less.
Engine changes are allowed when the client lacks the facts.
Proposal (consider-contrast): symbol graph with named bindings as boxes, unnamed steps as labelled edges, functions as role-tinted frames, server as a band.
Spidering covers data plus calls and state reads/writes and callers, not only value flow.
Start with a reasonable first screen; grow by keyboard shortcut or depth slider, never by many single clicks.
Components are frames like hooks or helpers in the Data lens; the Components lens stays for the render tree.
A route first screen reaches through the server boundary to the database.
Value flow is the bold main line with its operation labelled; calls and reads/writes are thin grey links that can be toggled.
First screen is the main path from origins to ends, about 25 symbols, with side branches as +N stubs that grow by key or slider.
Plain TS modules with no routes or components are an equal target.
Dial in the UX on a small reasonable example; use larger repos to build out the engine and find errors.
All reads of one binding (doc, doc(), doc() in Match when) are one symbol box; the pattern recurs widely.
Field reads merge into their symbol with the field name on the edge; symbol kind carries the strong color, frames neutral with a role word.

shape.appetite: One initiative: replace the Data lens box model and folding; walk, routes and Components lens unchanged.
shape.problem: The Data lens draws functions as grey component-like boxes and repeats one symbol across several boxes, hiding transforms, state and the server hop.
shape.recommended_shape: Symbol graph: one box per checker symbol per frame, bold labelled value-flow edges, thin toggled call/read links, role frames, server band, main path first with +/- and depth slider.
success_moves: Merge by symbolId sent through the contract, never by label
Prove the merge on a small fixture before visual-notes
Keep the old box model behind a view switch until the visual-notes check passes
Reuse function-effects facts for call and read links; no new walk semantics
Keep each merged edge opening to every original proof (#153)

first_proof.question: Does merging by checker symbol cut the box count enough to build a main-path first screen on symbols?
first_proof.artifact: anchor contract symbol field + anchorAdapter merge, run on a new small fixture and on visual-notes /docs/[id]
first_proof.decision_rule: A cut of a third or more on /docs/[id], with no wrong merges, means build on symbols; otherwise move main-path selection into the engine first.

rabbit_holes: Main-path selection needs a ranking the engine may not have
symbolId may be null or the callee symbol for accessor calls
Role detection for frames could drift into srcly-specific analysis edits
